sources.entry: iOScanX - Cocoa application for semi-automated iOS app analysis and evaluation.

summary.one_liner: iOScanX is a Cocoa macOS application that provides a guided, semi-automated workflow for analyzing and evaluating iOS apps, built on the ScanX framework.
summary.what_it_does: The app walks the user through four steps. First, it acquires a set of iOS apps, automatically decrypting and importing them from a jailbroken device connected over SSH via USB or Wi-Fi. Second, it imports and selects analysis modules, showing the metrics each module provides along with a short description. Third, it lets the user define and edit evaluation expressions built from those module metrics. Fourth, it presents the analysis results for review and can export them in the XML plist format.
use_cases: analyzing iOS apps from a jailbroken device
decrypting and importing iPhone apps over SSH
scoring iOS apps with custom metric expressions
exporting app analysis results as plist
notable: Guided four-step workflow from app acquisition to results review
Automatic decryption and import of apps from jailbroken devices over SSH (USB or Wi-Fi)
Pluggable analysis modules with listed metrics
Editable evaluation expressions built on module metrics
Results export in XML plist format
caveats: Requires a jailbroken iOS device for app acquisition, as the README describes device-based import
Built on the separate ScanX framework, which must be part of the same project ecosystem
README gives no setup or build instructions
